instruction: Delete the email account with the address "anonym-x2024@outlook.com" from my Thunderbird client

metadata.explanation: This variation asks the user to delete a specific Outlook email account from Thunderbird. The evaluator uses the same firefox_decrypt.py script to export account information to CSV, then verifies the account 'anonym-x2024@outlook.com' is no longer present in the unexpect list. This is a paraphrase variation that maintains the same evaluator logic as the original task.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses postconfig to extract current Thunderbird account state after deletion attempt via firefox_decrypt.py script
The check_csv metric properly verifies absence of the deleted account using the 'unexpect' pattern - returns 1.0 if account NOT found (success), 0.0 if found (failure)
Expected values correctly specify the account details (url: imap://outlook.office365.com, user: anonym-x2024@outlook.com) that should NOT exist after deletion
Parameter handling is correct - check_csv uses 'rules' parameter and accesses it directly as rules.get('unexpect'), not expected.get('rules')
Complete coverage - instruction requires deleting specific email account, evaluator verifies account no longer exists in Thunderbird profile
Verification logic is sound - postconfig re-extracts account information after task execution to capture current state
